paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the vocabulary size across a number of iterations for three languages: Spanish, Korean, and Japanese, along with an additional diagonal gray line. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Iterations" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500, with tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 100. The y-axis is labeled "Vocabulary Size" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 5000 with tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 1000. A solid gray line without markers extends linearly across the plot, starting at a value of 0 at 0 iterations and ending at exactly 5000 at 500 iterations. The Spanish data is represented by a main solid blue line without markers that starts at 0 and increases steadily to approximately 3300 at 500 iterations; it is surrounded by a cluster of fainter, lighter blue lines following a similar trajectory and ending between roughly 3100 and 3500. The Korean data is shown as a main solid orange line without markers, beginning at 0 and rising steadily to roughly 3050 at 500 iterations, accompanied by fainter orange lines that conclude between approximately 2800 and 3100. The Japanese data is depicted by a main solid green line without markers, starting at 0 and steadily climbing to around 3250 at 500 iterations, with corresponding fainter green lines ending in a spread between roughly 3100 and 3300.
